newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic sees integration on track.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic sees integration on track.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp, which completed its merger with NYNEX Corp on Thursday, said its management succession plans and estimates of cost savings from the combination remain on track.

At a press conference Friday in New York, Bell Atlantic executives also said they believe the company has a head start on other Baby Bells to gain regulatory approval to offer long- distance phone service in its 12-state local service region.

Ivan Seidenberg, the merged company's president and chief operating officer, said Bell Atlantic remains on track to acheive 1997 year cost reductions in line with current Wall Street estimates on potential cost savings from the merger.
The company has previously said it expected the merger to result in annualized savings in the range of $850 to $900 million per year over time.
"We have plans for the savings we will acheive this year and they are on track with what Wall Street has been estimating," Seidenberg said.

Bell Atlantic Chairman and Chief Executive Raymond W. Smith said the merged company is "uniquely positioned to grow revenues" versus industry peers, adding "It's more uniquely positioned to get into long distance than any of the other companies."

Responding to reporters' questions, Bell Atlantic executives said they believed the conditions agreed to with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to gain approval for the merger gave the company "a head-up" on long-distance entry.
These voluntary commitments are generally designed to lower barriers to competition in Bell Atlantic's local service region stretching from Maine to Virginia.
Regulators want such local service barriers to drop before they allow Bell Atlantic to offer long-distance services.
"We think they would look favorably" on a regulatory application to enter the long-distance market, one Bell Atlantic executive said, referring to the FCC.
The officials said the company has no plans to use the courts to win long-distance entry, a tactic that other Baby Bells, including SBC Communications Inc and Ameritech Corp, have pursued.
"We think we will be in long distance very soon," Smith said.
"The next issues for us (are) to move slowly into video and aggressively into long distance," Seidenberg said.
Discussing the executive succession plans for the company, Smith disputed a report that he might have hesitations about carrying through on making Seidenberg his successor.
"I think that there was a misunderstanding," Smith said in referring to a recent Wall Street Journal article on the issue. "What I am saying is that there are no guarantees in life."
But he quickly stressed that, "Ivan is my candidate. He is the person the board has accepted," Smith said, adding that the Seidenberg's employment agreement was "pretty air-tight."

Smith is scheduled to remain chairman and chief executive for one year after the merger is completed. Seidenberg, the former chief executive with NYNEX Corp, would take over from Smith as chief executive, and as chairman some months later.
Bell Atlantic stock was down 15/16 of a point in New York Stock Exchange trading to 75 in early afternoon.
